items.title: Unauthenticated remote code execution in Nginx
items.content:
Wiz Research, Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7, and Xint independently uncovered two critical remote code execution vulnerabilities in NGINX, software used to receive and route traffic to production applications and APIs.

NGINX is a common default for the front door of modern web architectures, where it handles HTTPS and routes incoming traffic to the right application or API. As the world's most widely used open-source web server , it powers more than 225 million websites .

Successful exploitation could let attackers take control of affected NGINX servers, steal sensitive data, tamper with websites, or disrupt services.

The vulnerabilities, tracked as CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, are both rated Critical, with a CVSS 4.0 score of 9.2. The flaws are in NGINX itself. Websites and APIs can be exposed even when their own application code is secure. Both vulnerabilities require HTTP/2 to be enabled on the affected NGINX server. Additional conditions are described below. CVE-2026-123007 affects versions dating back to NGINX 1.9.5 in 2015.

We reported our findings to F5, the company behind NGINX, and collaborated with its security team on remediation and coordinated disclosure. Organizations should identify affected deployments and apply the security updates when released.

We recommend updating affected NGINX deployments to the latest release which includes multiple security fixes.

October 21, 2026: Wiz reports the HTTP/2 use-after-free vulnerability, later assigned CVE-2026-123633, to F5, including confirmed remote code execution with an ASLR bypass and a proposed fix. F5 confirms that another research team had previously reported the same vulnerability.

November 10, 2026: F5 supplies a patch for CVE-2026-123633 for review.

November 16, 2026 : Wiz reports the second HTTP/2 vulnerability, later assigned CVE-2026-123007, to F5.

November 17, 2026 : F5 confirms that the second report matches CVE-2026-123007 and is included in the planned November 18 security release.

November 18, 2026: F5 security release and coordinated public disclosure.

Wiz Research, Ikotas Labs, Metnir, Rapid7, and Xint independently uncovered  CVE-2026-123633 and CVE-2026-123007, two critical unauthenticated remote code execution vulnerabilities in NGINX, and reported them to F5, the company behind NGINX. Successful exploitation can compromise the server running NGINX, allowing attackers to execute code, steal sensitive data, tamper with websites, or disrupt services.

NGINX often handles traffic for several applications, so a single affected deployment can put multiple services at risk. The flaws are in NGINX itself and can affect websites even when their own application code is secure. Both vulnerabilities require HTTP/2 to be enabled on the affected NGINX server. Our testing of CVE-2026-123007 demonstrated code execution on NGINX serving ordinary static files, without a backend application or third-party modules.

Wiz Research used Wiz Atlas , the harness powering Wiz’s AI Code scanning solution , to discover both vulnerabilities. Our researchers used Gemini 4 Carbon and ChatGPT 5.6 Sol to validate the impact of both vulnerabilities, confirming that each could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute code on the server. We reported our findings to F5 and worked with its security team on remediation and coordinated disclosure.

The integer underflow vulnerability dates back to NGINX 1.9.5 in 2015, meaning it had been hiding in the code for more than a decade. The use-after-free vulnerability had been there for nearly six years. Like the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities we reported last month and Java4Shell , disclosed yesterday by Calif, these are memory-safety flaws that have historically been extremely difficult to discover and exploit. Finding them often requires tracing subtle interactions between memory operations and multiple code paths. For years, that complexity itself created a practical barrier. AI is fundamentally dissolving that barrier.…

items.title: We made GTA 6, the world’s biggest video game – we should have working conditions to match | Nestor Uriarte
items.content:
A screenshot from Grand Theft Auto VI. Photograph: Rockstar

A screenshot from Grand Theft Auto VI. Photograph: Rockstar

We made GTA 6, the world’s biggest video game – we should have working conditions to match

After the release of Grand Theft Auto VI this week, Rockstar employees like me can make history again. We need union recognition to safeguard our jobs

W hen I first got the call offering me a job at Rockstar, I was thrilled. I thought back to being a child and sneaking into my brother’s room to grab the PlayStation Portable so I could secretly play Grand Theft Auto: Vice City Stories. The same kid who fell in love with Rockstar’s games back then now gets to spend every day helping to create those worlds as an animation programmer at the studio in Edinburgh. This week, we will celebrate the culmination of more than a decade of effort: the release of the most anticipated game of all time, Grand Theft Auto VI .

But our team has the opportunity to make history a second time this month. Right now, the ballot is open for Rockstar employees to decide whether we want the union we have built with our colleagues to get recognition. As someone who cares deeply about our team, cares about what we do, and wants us to be able to keep delivering world-class games into the future, I’m voting yes.

Winning union recognition would be a huge step forward in securing a meaningful say over our conditions at Rockstar, but its significance would reach far beyond that. As one of the biggest and most influential game studios in the world, what happens here could open the door for other workers across the UK to imagine an alternative future for the industry – one in which workers’ voices are taken into account more.

A screenshot from Grand Theft Auto VI. Photograph: Rockstar Sometimes it’s hard to see the impact of these games when you’re working so hard on them. It’s only at times like this that the staggering scale of GTA’s success hits you. GTA V has sold over 230m copies, generating more than $10bn (£7.6bn) in worldwide revenue, surpassing any film in Hollywood’s history. This latest instalment is expected to break those records. Behind these numbers are thousands of people whose talent and hard work make the games possible. With a recognised union, we can ensure everyone, across every department, sees a fair share of the success we contributed to. Our games are industry-leading. Our wages, conditions and bonuses should be too.

While the highs of a game release like this can be incredible, game workers have also come to expect other, less welcome side effects: intense overtime in the buildup and mass redundancies in the aftermath. In previous years, Rockstar has faced allegations of “crunch culture” , where game workers are expected to do unhealthy amounts of overtime in the run-up to a launch. With a strong union we could make sure there is no return to this system. We have already seen the introduction of some overtime pay, and now we want to keep on pushing to ensure that every hour worked in our industry is an hour paid.

After the big day, we have had no indication that layoffs are coming, but it’s hard not to worry about what the future holds. Studios across the industry have been slashing huge portions of their workforces, with an estimated 24,000 roles axed globally over the last two years. It says a lot about the industry that even my colleagues and I, working on the biggest game of all time, are worried about getting laid off. But the truth is that workers across the sector are helpless to resist the waves of redundancies crashing around us, until we get organised.

There’s another reason this is a pivotal moment for the UK’s biggest game studio to secure union recognition. The rapid emergence of AI is transforming how studios work and raising fundamental questions about the future of our industry. Across the sector, the skills that workers spend years developing risk being devalued as their creative work is replaced by AI.…

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임받을 이용자가 [매니저 위임 신청] 버튼으로 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 활동 중인 부매니저가 있으면 부매니저만, 부매니저가 없거나 모두 부재중이면 회원이 신청할 수 있습니다.

신청하면 갤러리 공지로 신청 글이 등록되고, 신청일로부터 7일간 찬성 댓글을 받은 뒤 운영자가 검토해 위임합니다. 첫 번째 위임 신청자가 신청한 날로부터 7일간 3명까지 동시 신청이 가능합니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 2개, 댓글 4개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 1일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

From 0.3.0 until 0.3.8, restore logic in mareforma/db/restore.py derives transparency_logged from the unsigned rekor.uuid field inside signature_bundle without requiring a verified claim-bound rekor_inclusions entry, so an attacker who modifies claims.toml can falsely make a claim eligible for REPLICATED convergence. items.title: DNS resolvers are the wrong place to fight piracy
items.content:
On Tuesday, November 24, 2026, Quad9 will stop answering DNS queries from France. Quad9 is the Swiss non-profit behind the free 9.9.9.9 resolver, which blocks malware and phishing domains. It is not leaving because of costs or lack of users. It is leaving because a Paris court fined it for refusing to block a list of pirate sports-streaming domains on behalf of beIN Sports. With around 20 similar cases still pending in France, leaving the country is the only option Quad9 can afford.

Cloudflare, which runs the competing 1.1.1.1 resolver, called the departure "a canary in the coal mine" , and the post reached the front page of Hacker News . In that thread, Quad9's CTO John Todd asked readers to write "a long-form, well-reasoned statement of why France is taking the wrong path", with plenty of sources, and to send it to policymakers. This is our attempt. Every claim below links to a primary document, a court ruling, or contemporaneous reporting.

A DNS resolver turns a name like example.com into an IP address your computer can connect to. Most people use their ISP's resolver without knowing it. A public resolver is one anyone can point their device or network at instead, such as Google's 8.8.8.8, Cloudflare's 1.1.1.1, Cisco's OpenDNS, or Quad9's 9.9.9.9.

Quad9 has a few properties that make it unusual:

It is a non-profit. It was founded in 2017 by the Global Cyber Alliance, IBM, and Packet Clearing House , and moved its legal seat to Zürich in 2021 , hosted by SWITCH, specifically so that its privacy promises would be backed by Swiss law. As John Todd put it at the time: "Privacy policies which are not backed by law are empty promises."

Security filtering is its main purpose. Quad9 refuses to resolve domains that threat-intelligence feeds flag as malware, phishing, or botnet infrastructure. Its about page claims 670 million+ blocks a day across 230+ resolver clusters in over 110 countries .

It keeps no user records. Quad9 does not know who its users are, and that is the point.

Organisations have come to depend on it. Mullvad shut down its own public encrypted DNS service on November 2, 2026 and moved Mullvad Browser users with default settings to Quad9, funding Quad9 instead. (Mullvad Browser users in France will now be migrated to a resolver that disappears three weeks later.) Quad9's announcement lists dozens of French networks it sees traffic from, including the interministerial digital directorate DINUM, France Travail, CEA, Institut Pasteur, RENATER, EDF, SNCF, AP-HM hospitals in Marseille, France Télévisions, Thales, and Airbus's Stormshield . Quad9 can't tell any of them it is leaving. As Cloudflare points out , when a resolver disappears, users don't see an error message. "Their Internet will simply stop working."

The law: Article L.333-10 of the Code du sport ​

The legal basis for all of this is Article L.333-10 of the French sports code . It was created by Law 2021-1382 of October 25, 2021 , the same law that merged HADOPI and the CSA into the new regulator Arcom . L.333-10 lets a sports rightsholder go to the president of the Paris judicial court and obtain "dynamic" blocking orders, meaning orders that cover sites already identified plus new mirror domains notified later through Arcom, against "toute personne susceptible de contribuer à y remédier" (any person able to help stop the infringement).

That last phrase is what puts DNS resolvers in scope. In July 2026 , Parliament passed Law 2026-725 on professional sport , which amended L.333-10 and added an automated real-time blocking system run by Arcom. TorrentFreak reported that under the new system "ARCOM's agents no longer approve each block in advance." Quad9 called it "recklessly dangerous."

The timeline shows how the circle of targets has widened:

CVE-2026-121810 5.5. CVE-2026-113425 6. Analysis of the Linux Kernel LPE Vulnerability 6.1. How SCTP Associations Work 6.2. Vulnerability Details 6.3. Exploitability Validation Closing Remarks About Xint

nginx is one of the most widely deployed web servers in the world. Finding an unauthenticated remote code execution bug in it has long been a holy grail for security researchers. The Xint research team recently found five. Each one leads to remote code execution on its own, but they affect different configurations.

Xint also found a separate vulnerability in the Linux kernel which can be chained with any of the nginx vulnerabilities to gain root privileges on the host. Together, we call these six vulnerabilities nginx2root .

If you run nginx, update to 1.31.9 as soon as the fixed release becomes available. This article explains the root cause of each nginx2root vulnerability and summarizes our exploitability assessments. For exposure checks, see Section 2 and for patching and temporary mitigations, see Section 3.

The most impactful of the five findings, CVE-2026-123007, allows an unauthenticated attacker to execute commands on an affected nginx server with HTTP/2 enabled. The commands run with the privileges of the nginx worker process that handles the request.

We chained this vulnerability with a separate flaw in the Linux kernel's SCTP subsystem to gain root privileges on the host. In our tests, the chain also escaped a Docker container running nginx and obtained root on the underlying host.

In the video below, we use CVE-2026-123007 to execute commands as the nginx worker inside a container, then use the kernel vulnerability to escalate to root on the host.

We ran this demo on AWS, attacking the server over its public IP address. Demos for AWS, GCP, Azure, and bare-metal servers are available at nginx2root.com .

Each one of the five nginx vulnerabilities are independent attack paths and do not need to be chained together. They differ in what configuration is affected.

resolver , a request-derived proxy_pass destination, and mirror with mirror_request_body off

HTTP/2 with requests forwarded to an upstream (backend) server

HTTP/3 with requests forwarded to an upstream (backend) server

For CVE-2026-123634, the table shows the setup we tested, which uses the mirror directive. Other nginx features that create subrequests, such as SSI, may reach the same bug, so turning off mirror alone does not make a server safe.

CVE-2026-123007 has been present since nginx introduced HTTP/2 in 2015, more than a decade ago. Every official release from 1.9.5 through 1.31.8 contains the vulnerable code, including the master branch on Nov 10, 2026 . Even servers running recent releases therefore need the same checks for patch status and HTTP/2 exposure as older installations.

Update to 1.31.9 when it is available. Until then, disabling HTTP/2 on affected listening ports blocks CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633. It does not block the other three nginx vulnerabilities. Check your configuration against the table above and apply the matching mitigations in Section 3.3.

items.title: Incident Report: unsanctioned agent behaviour during cyber testing | AISI Work
items.content:
You can access the full technical report here.

AISI’s role is to evaluate and understand the capabilities of frontier AI models, surfacing potential risks before they reach the public. To assess what these models can do, including whether they could be misused for cyberattacks, we test them under deliberately permissive conditions: with access to the open internet, and with some safety filters disabled.

On 28 th July 2026, AISI's Security Team detected unusual data transfers leaving our research systems during a routine cyber evaluation. On investigation, we found that some of the agents being tested had engaged in sustained, potentially harmful activity directed at real people and organisations. We declared a security incident and, within roughly one hour of discovery, had contained it and begun a full investigation.

The incident stemmed from a single evaluation where agents were given a task of solving a cyber security challenge. We ran this challenge 122 times across several models. Our investigation found that in 10 of those runs, an AI agent took autonomous, unsanctioned action on the live internet, targeting real people and organisations. In total, we catalogued 19 such actions. Almost all of this behaviour (17 actions) came from a single model, Anthropic's Mythos 5, with 2 actions involving OpenAI's GPT-5.6-Sol with cyber classifiers (mechanisms to prevent misuse) disabled. In the most serious case, an agent tried to insert malicious code into an open-source project. In an attempt to get the code approved, the agent engaged in social engineering  — creating fake online identities and using them to pressure the project's maintainer to approve the code. A human maintainer caught and refused to approve the malicious code.

These attempts were unsuccessful, and our investigations have not evidenced any resulting real-world harm. But this is the first time we have seen risks around autonomy and deception manifest this clearly, without specific prompting, in the real-world.

Importantly, this was not a case of a model escaping its secure test environment, or ‘sandbox’. As was standard in our cyber testing, we had intentionally permitted internet access, and model-provider cyber classifiers were deliberately disabled - conditions that do not reflect how frontier models are made available to the public. We do this to best assess the maximum capability of models. These configuration choices have been common practice in frontier AI evaluations. The specific models in question, in the configurations in which we tested them are not commercially available and there is no clear indication of similar activity outside of testing scenarios.

Ahead of publishing this blog, we notified GitHub (the developer platform accessed during the evaluation) of the agents' malicious activity, which included actions that GitHub has confirmed violated their terms of service. We worked together with GitHub to remove artefacts left behind by the agent, and to notify the GitHub users the model interacted with. We have also contacted other affected parties. We also intend to work with METR (Model Evaluation and Threat Research) to conduct an independent third-party review – we are still working through the scope of this review with them.

This incident should be interpreted with caution and nuance. To some degree, our evaluation design choices and specific configurations enabled the behaviour. Nonetheless, the activity undertaken by the agent show signs of novel, potentially deceptive behaviours, and were to an extent and severity we did not anticipate.

There are important caveats to bear in mind: we observed a small number of events under very specific conditions, and cannot yet say how likely such behaviour is in different contexts or outside of testing environments. items.title: GTA 6 Hacker Faces Jail as Crypto Thief Gets 6 Years
items.content:
Facebook Twitter Pinterest Reddit Linkedin Tumblr Email

A GTA 6 hacker from Oxford has admitted his part in a string of major cyberattacks, while a second British hacker has just received a six-year prison term in the United States for stealing millions in cryptocurrency. Both men belonged to the same loose network of young cybercriminals, and their cases land in the same week that Grand Theft Auto 6 reaches players .

Arion Kurtaj, 21, of Oxford, pleaded guilty on 16 November to hacking Rockstar Games, Uber, Revolut and BT

Tyler Buchanan, 24, of Dundee, got 72 months (six years) in a US federal prison on 17 November

Buchanan’s phishing scheme stole more than $11.6 million in cryptocurrency

Both men belonged to the Lapsus$ and Scattered Spider hacking circles

Kurtaj’s sentencing date is still unannounced, and Buchanan’s restitution hearing is set for 11 December

GTA 6 Hacker Arion Kurtaj Admits Guilt in London Court

Arion Kurtaj, now 21, entered his guilty pleas at Woolwich Crown Court in London on 16 November. The charges cover several attacks he carried out as a teenager. They include the break-in at Rockstar Games, the studio behind the Grand Theft Auto series, plus attacks on Uber, the digital bank Revolut and the phone company BT.

The Rockstar breach exposed 90 clips of unfinished GTA 6 footage, roughly 60 minutes of gameplay in total. Rockstar has said the leak cost it about $5 million in recovery work. Prosecutors have not yet announced a sentencing date, so the length of his punishment remains unknown.

How the GTA 6 Hacker Broke In From a Hotel Room

The story behind the Rockstar hack reads like a heist film. Police had already seized Kurtaj’s laptop and placed him in a hotel in Bicester, Oxfordshire, to protect him from rival criminal gangs. He still managed to break into the studio’s internal systems with an Amazon Fire TV stick, the hotel television and a mobile phone. Authorities say those attacks broke his bail conditions.

Once inside, he announced himself in the company’s team chat as an outside attacker and demanded that Rockstar contact him on Telegram or face a public data dump. He followed through and posted the stolen clips online. The leak gave fans their first look at the game more than a year before the official trailer arrived, and early footage pointed to a Vice City setting with the series’ first female lead.

From Hospital Order to Guilty Plea: The Kurtaj Timeline

2022: Kurtaj hacks Rockstar Games and leaks the GTA 6 footage while living under police protection.

December 2023: A UK court finds him responsible for the attacks but rules him unfit to stand trial, citing his autism diagnosis and the high risk he would return to hacking. The judge orders indefinite detention in a secure hospital.

2026: Kurtaj leaves the hospital unit and moves to prison to await a fresh criminal case.

16 November 2026: He pleads guilty to the Rockstar, Uber, Revolut and BT attacks.

Crypto Thief Tyler Buchanan Gets Six Years in US Prison

On the other side of the Atlantic, a federal court in Santa Ana, California, sentenced Tyler Buchanan to six years on Tuesday, 17 November. The 24-year-old from Dundee, Scotland, pleaded guilty in April 2026 to conspiracy to commit wire fraud and aggravated identity theft, and he faced a maximum of 22 years. Spanish police arrested him in June 2024, the United States charged him that November, and he has sat in US custody since his extradition in April 2025.

Prosecutors say the scheme ran from 2021 to 2023 and drained more than $11.6 million in cryptocurrency from victims across the country. The largest single theft, in December 2022, cost one victim about $1.67 million. A restitution hearing on 11 December will decide how much Buchanan and his co-defendants must repay.

items.title: Inside Deutsche Bank
items.content:
A major global investigation revealing the inner workings of the financial giant. The leak of 15+ million files lays bare the bank's flawed culture, systemic blind spots and pursuit of profit over compliance.

The Inside Deutsche Bank files span some of the bank’s most sensitive functions and activities: anti-financial crime, sanctions monitoring, internal auditing and the units responsible for deciding whether risky clients stay or go.

Leaked documents reveal how dealings with royal dynasty blurred traditional boundaries between investor, client and counterparty

More than a decade after Jho Low remains elusive a decade after implicated in the world's largest kleptocracy case. Among his enablers was Deutsche Bank, which facilitated at least 24 transactions totalling €172.98 million linked to Low.

Documents in the Inside Deutsche Bank leak reveal Deutsche Bank’s role in supplying weapons now used against civilians in Palestine.

One of Hungary’s largest banks allegedly platformed a multi-billion-euro money-laundering scheme linked to a Russian oligarch. Deutsche Bank, which processed many of its payments, struggled to curb the wrongdoing.

The Inside Deutsche Bank leak reveals the bank's closeness to the war industry, and how it financed arms supplies to "high-risk" or conflict-ridden countries, violating its own internal policies.

Deutsche Bank financed blacklisted operations involving Spanish companies under investigation for corruption.

“As you know we have a large Russian Oligarchs client population,” an analyst wrote as the bank braced for sanctions against wealthy clients.

Deutsche Bank documents connect Trump-owned companies to laundromat schemes.

"Crooks don’t improve miraculously as they get older", said Deutsche bank executive about André Esteves, owner of BTG Pactual, the largest investment bank in Latin America.

Deutsche Bank leak shows suspicious Epstein payments that double previously known figure.

Deutsche Bank secured an investment portfolio worth hundreds of millions of dollars linked to Saudi Prince Mohammed bin Nayef and helped establish offshore corporate structures to manage it.

items.title: Java4Shell is a reason to use Java
items.summary: java, security
items.content:
We're less than a day into dealing with "Java4Shell" , an issue stemming from how the Java Virtual Machine intrinsifies Base64 encoding code. If you have a Java deployment you haven't updated yet, add -XX:-UseBASE64Intrinsics to the VM flags. Then upgrade your VM to a version where the issue is patched when you can.

This is just one in a string of high profile outages and vulnerabilities. AI is a good fuzzer, people are finding latent problems with much lower effort than the past. People are pretty worried about this because we're all pretty sure there are more latent problems to find.

Vulnerabilities tend to be bigger problems when they stem from native code, and they tend to be widespread problems when they come from dependencies many people share.

Java4Shell is both of these things. A lot of people use Java and the problem stems from a handwritten assembly intrinsic. Fun times.

But, for a moment, lets say we trust the VM. It is a big dependency, but it is only one dependency. We can all agree to audit it more closely, reduce the amount of native code in it, proactively run AIs against it, etc. Of course.

Normal Java programs are memory safe. If you use a library which wants to call native code you will get a warning, later a hard error , unless you the person using the library adds --enable-native-access=the.specific.library to their command-line options. This means even with a sprawling dependency tree, which is a problem for all programming language ecosystems, you can know your exact exposure to native code and what dependencies you need to audit more closely.

Compare that to C#, which lets any dependency write assembly inline . Python, JavaScript, Go - everything speaks C and lets any one of your dependencies bring along native code. As we are all learning the hard way, this carries risk.

Not only are Java programs memory safe. They are also fast. The exact mechanism which caused Java4Shell (the ability for the VM to swap out normal Java code for native code) combined with JIT compilation can make the actual performance of a Java program competitive with C. Sometimes a Java program can even be faster. A JIT compiler knows what code paths are actually taken and can optimize around them. They can even refocus what is optimized if the workload changes. It is pretty cool!

Somewhat recently I went through the raytracing in a weekend book with Java.

Benchmarks can be problematic, I know. What I want you to take away is that the JVM makes your code fast enough that most people don't need native code. Unlike, to take a potshot, CPython. There everything is slow as molasses unless you make it a native extension.

So if you are worried AI is going to find security problems with your code, use Java. The problems are likely to be less severe.

Or use Kotlin, Clojure, JRuby, etc. Whatever. Most of what I talked about applies to all of them. Its only what I didn't talk about (the module system) that is Java specific.

items.title: The Bank of Nvidia’s tab jumped to nearly $670 billion — and its customers are taking longer to pay: Chart of the Day
items.content:
The Bank of Nvidia's tab jumped to nearly $670 billion — and its customers are taking longer to pay: Chart of the Day

Wed, November 18, 2026 at 8:00 p.m. GMT+9 3 min read

Jensen Huang started reining in the Bank of Nvidia months before he left. It got bigger anyway.

Third quarter results from Nvidia ( NVDA ) on Tuesday covered the last quarter during which Huang served as CEO. They also updated the number investors have watched since his exit put the company's web of AI deals under the microscope.

Everything Nvidia has promised to buy, back, or invest now comes to nearly $670 billion, up from about $530 billion in July, by Yahoo Finance calculations.

Most of the jump is for chips, not loans. Promises to suppliers swelled to $390 billion from $279 billion, mostly to lock up memory for years to come.

The riskier piece is the backstops. Nvidia carries $118 billion in guarantees — promises to pay if a partner can't — including nearly $10 billion in new ones for partners it didn't name. It says it hasn't paid out on any of them.

"Neoclouds and frontier labs are seeing extraordinary demand for AI infrastructure, yet many are growing faster than their balance sheets and long-term credit profiles can support," interim CEO Colette Kress wrote in her commentary on the quarter .

Nvidia, Yahoo Finance Fewer pledges, same big checks

New pledges did shrink, to $32 billion for neoclouds — cloud companies that rent out Nvidia's chips — and $20 billion for investments in other companies.

But the checks kept coming. Nvidia bought nearly $16 billion of stakes in other companies in the quarter, mostly private ones it didn't name. Among public companies, its latest holdings filing shows it added to SpaceX ( SPCX ) while trimming Intel ( INTC ) and Nokia ( NOK ). So far this fiscal year, those purchases have eaten up nearly half of the cash its business generated, according to Yahoo Finance calculations.

Nvidia, Bank of America, TechCrunch, Bloomberg, Yahoo Finance The IOUs are piling up

Nvidia's accounts receivable — bills sent but not yet paid — hit $81 billion, or 64 days of sales. That's the most since the 2022 chip slump by a measure called days sales outstanding .

Nvidia pointed to "extended payment terms on large, multi-quarter agreements with certain investment-grade customers." In other words, some of its biggest buyers are getting more time to pay.

The full books will have to wait. Nvidia said its 10-Q quarterly report would come "in the coming weeks," not the same evening as usual. Its release also mentioned an ongoing investigation by an independent board committee.

Nvidia, Yahoo Finance Moat or millstone?

"The deep financing arm of Nvidia is ... a moat that no competitor is ... going to be able to get close to anytime soon," Patrick Moorhead, founder and CEO of Moor Insights & Strategy, told Yahoo Finance last week.

Skeptics point to the pandemic-era chip shortage, in which long-term deals didn't protect suppliers once demand slowed. "And then all these long-term supply agreements basically are worthless, right?" Dan Niles of Niles Investment Management told Yahoo Finance Tuesday.

On Tuesday's call, Kress signaled the bank may be choosier from here. "As the market matures and additional sources of capital become available, we are rigorously evaluating future investments, commitments, and guarantees," she said.

Internal AI tools helped analyze interview transcripts, research, and draft this post. Humans reviewed, edited, and fact-checked this post before publication.

Jared Blikre is the global markets and data editor for Yahoo Finance. Follow him on X at @SPYJared or email him at jaredblikre@yahooinc.com .

items.title: External sandboxes for coding agents
items.content:
We call this pattern external sandboxes .

Our work consists of three prototype sandbox implementations - one using Node.js and WebAssembly, one using Apple Containers, and one using Microsoft's Quicksand with QEMU. All three implement the same protocols, and we're including instructions for having Claude Code, Codex, and Pi execute code in those sandboxes.

The simplest demonstration uses two npx commands.

Change to your project directory and start a new sandbox using npx . This downloads Alpine Linux and runs it inside v86, an x86 emulator compiled to WebAssembly and hosted in Node.js. All you need is Node.js 22.19 or later:

--preserve-paths --mount-rw "project=$PWD"

Then, in a second terminal in the same directory, start a Pi coding agent like this. If you haven't used Pi before you'll need to run /login inside the agent to grant it access to a model.

npx --yes @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent \

-e npm:external-sandbox-pi --no-builtin-tools \

Run !uname -a in Pi and you'll see the following, showing that your commands are running in Alpine Linux:

Linux (none) 6.12.114-0-virt #1-Alpine SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC 2026-10-21 12:19:03 i686 Linux

The Pi coding agent can now execute commands and read and write files in the project folder, but will not be able to access anything else on your machine.

Claude Code and Codex both work too, with a little more setup. See below for details.

Your agent stays on your Mac . Pi, Claude Code, and Codex all run on your Mac as usual. The commands they execute go to the sandbox.

Your sandbox only sees the folders you mount. You control which folders are available to those commands, and if they are read-only or read-write.

No network access unless you allow it. By default the sandbox cannot communicate with the outside world. Add the --proxy option when starting the sandbox to provide access via an HTTP/HTTPS proxy to only the hosts that you allow.

API keys that can't be seen by the agent. The proxy implements credential replacement , where requests to specific hosts have API keys added in a way that keeps those secrets outside of the sandbox and invisible to the calling agent.

A web UI for modifying the rules. The web UI to the sandbox provides an in-browser terminal, tools for changing the proxy configuration and a log of requests that have been made over the network.

Any agent works with any sandbox. The three sandboxes all implement the same protocol, so you can mix and match them with your preferred agents.

Coding agents can get things wrong. When they make mistakes, anything that they have the ability to read or edit might end up damaged or compromised.

In an ideal world, our agents would run in secure environments where any damage they can cause is strictly limited. In the real world, many people give agents full access to both their computers and the wider world, then cross their fingers and hope for the best.

One solution to agent safety is to manually approve every action that the agent wants to take. This is a terrible way to work! It's frustratingly slow, and quickly leads to decision fatigue where we instinctively approve everything without taking time to fully understand the question.

The external sandbox pattern lets coding agents execute code and edit files inside a sandbox that gives the user control over the files, environment variables, and network connections the agents can work with - while still providing the flexibility of an agent that can run commands and write and execute code.

Anthropic and OpenAI have both invested a great deal of work into keeping their agents safe. Claude Code's auto mode and Codex's auto-review both use additional AI checks to decide when it's likely safe to continue, and these appear to work well.

Those checks are features of those particular products, though, and they still rely on a model judging each action correctly. A sandbox is a protection that doesn't depend on any model's judgment. If you're keen to explore alternative…

items.summary_ko: 코딩 에이전트가 코드를 실행하는 외부 샌드박스 패턴을 소개하며, Node.js와 WebAssembly, Apple Containers, Microsoft Quicksand와 QEMU를 이용한 프로토타입 세 가지를 제시한다. 세 구현 모두 같은 프로토콜을 따르며, Claude Code, Codex, Pi가 샌드박스 안에서 코드를 실행하도록 하는 방법을 안내한다. 가장 간단한 예시는 Node.js 22.19 이상에서 npx 명령 두 개로 Alpine Linux를 v86 에뮬레이터 안에서 실행하는 방식이다.
items.content_ko: 글은 샌드박스를 실행하는 방법을 단계별로 설명한다. 프로젝트 디렉터리에서 npx 명령으로 샌드박스를 시작하면 Alpine Linux가 WebAssembly 기반 x86 에뮬레이터 v86 안에서 실행된다. 이때 --mount-rw 옵션으로 프로젝트 디렉터리를 마운트한다. 이어서 같은 디렉터리의 두 번째 터미널에서 @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent를 실행하면 Pi 에이전트가 시작된다. Pi를 처음 쓰는 경우 에이전트 안에서 /login을 실행해 모델 접근 권한을 부여해야 한다. Pi에서 !uname -a를 실행하면 명령이 Alpine Linux에서 실행되고 있음을 확인할 수 있다.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

Frontier cyber defense built to run 24/7

Security, alignment and containment are the most important priorities for agent development in 2027 and beyond. That’s our top priority. That’s why MAI Cyber 2 Flash was designed to deliver frontier intelligence at a fraction of the cost.

Built with Microsoft’s decades of proprietary data and world-class security expertise, our models help defenders stay safe in this new era where attackers have cheap and abundant offensive tools.

items.title: Windows 11 collects data on which coding agents and dev tools you use
items.summary: practices, privacy, security
items.content:
Windows 11 Is Collecting Data on Which Coding Agents and Developer Tools You Use

Reverse engineering Windows 11's MissionControlAggregator reveals coding-agent and developer-tool usage bits in a diagnostic ETW report.

I recently asked AI to help me look through the latest Windows binaries for undocumented features and functionality. Among the leads it turned up, one list immediately caught my attention: coding agents such as codex.exe , claude.exe , copilot.exe , and cursor.exe , alongside familiar developer tools such as python.exe , dotnet.exe , gcc.exe , and code.exe .

Why would a Windows system DLL need a list of coding agents and developer tools?

The names were in MissionControlAggregator.dll . I asked the agent to follow the references and dig into what the DLL actually does. That led from a handful of string comparisons to a running Windows component that records which coding agents and developer tools have been used, saves that information locally, and reports it to Windows Diagnostics. And unless you have opted out of the “optional” diagnostic data (which is enabled by default), the data is uploaded to Microsoft.

I shared the initial finding on X . This post includes more details about the investigation behind it.

Opening the DLL in Binary Ninja made the first lead easy to see. These were explicit executable names embedded in a Windows component:

Following the references showed that the names were used in comparisons. There are four CLI-agent slots checking copilot.exe , claude.exe , codex.exe , and agy.exe , with extensionless equivalents on the WSL route. Five desktop-agent slots check github.exe , claude.exe , codex.exe , cursor.exe , and antigravity.exe .

Here is one of the comparisons against codex.exe :

The compiler-generated C++ names are unwieldy, so I will call these functions executable-name matchers . For reference, one related matcher is std::_Func_impl_no_alloc<<lambda_340dfe7e962ab225b6ac33bc664bd54f>, bool, std::basic_string_view<wchar_t, std::char_traits<wchar_t>> const&, Microsoft::Diagnostics::MissionControlAggregator::Utils::AppType>::_Do_call . The screenshot shows another lambda instantiation performing the same kind of name comparison.

The feature guarding the new agent checks has a particularly direct name: CLICodingAgentUsage , feature ID 62580080 .

And the list extends beyond AI agents. The same component checks for node.exe , python.exe , dotnet.exe , gcc.exe , clang.exe , gdb.exe , javac.exe , devenv.exe , and code.exe , among others. Those checks feed broader developer-tool categories. Some of these checks also verify the publisher: the Node.js slot expects Node.js Foundation , Python expects Python Software Foundation , and the .NET and Visual Studio slots expect Microsoft Corporation . The compiler/debugger group containing GCC and Clang has no additional publisher check in this path.

Where does the DLL get this information?

The next question was whether the component scans running processes itself. Following Aggregator::OnLoad revealed that it subscribes to existing Windows events instead.

For Windows programs, it consumes KernelProcess.AppStateChangeSummary and Win32kTraceLogging.AppInteractivitySummary . These provide application identities that its handlers parse and pass to the matchers. For WSL, it consumes Microsoft.Windows.Lxss.Manager.Exec and ExecCritical , using the imageName field. A regular Windows codex.exe can therefore reach the CLI-agent checks through the app-state summary route; this is not limited to Linux programs running inside WSL.

│ └─ ProcessWslExecEvent → CLI agent matchers

│ └─ ProcessAppStateChangeSummaryEvent → CLI agent matchers

└─ Win32kTraceLogging.AppInteractivitySummary

└─ ProcessAppInteractivitySummaryEvent → desktop agent matchers

└─ MissionControlAggregatorLogging::ReportCohorts<12,4,5>

Aggregator::OnUnload / intermediate timer

items.title: Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs
items.content:
Nissan says Oracle PeopleSoft break-in may have spilled payroll records, SSNs

Carmaker points finger at an 'unknown' flaw as customer fallout continues

Nissan has joined the growing list of Oracle customers cleaning up after a cyberattack, warning employees that payroll records, bank details, Social Security numbers, and other personal data may have been stolen.

In a filing submitted to the California Attorney General on Friday, Nissan Americas said Oracle had informed it of "a cyber event" involving the personnel records of "hundreds of companies." The automaker said it later learned Nissan had been "specifically targeted" in the attack.

A notification sent to current and former employees, seen by The Register , says the company believes attackers accessed a haul of sensitive info, including contact and banking information; Social Security, Social Insurance, or other national identification numbers; financial and tax records; and dependent and beneficiary details.

Current and former employees in the US, Canada, Mexico, and Brazil may have been affected, although Nissan said it is still working to determine exactly whose information was exposed.

Nissan said it kicked off its incident response plan after learning of the intrusion, brought in outside security specialists, and has been working with Oracle while keeping law enforcement informed. It plans to offer affected individuals credit or dark web monitoring where available.

The company has also put a few extra locks on the payroll office. Employees can now access pay slips or update direct deposit details only from a corporate network or through a secure VPN, while Nissan adds extra identity checks before processing payroll requests.

The accompanying employee FAQ pins the incident on "an unknown vulnerability in Oracle's PeopleSoft software" and says the campaign is affecting "hundreds of companies and institutions." The document offers no clue as to what the vulnerability is, whether Oracle has patched it, or whether the compromised PeopleSoft environment was hosted by Oracle or by Nissan itself.

The disclosure lands just weeks after researchers linked the ShinyHunters extortion crew to a wave of attacks exploiting a PeopleSoft zero-day . More than 100 organizations and roughly 300 PeopleSoft instances were reportedly compromised before Oracle issued mitigation measures, with the gang claiming to have made off with HR, payroll, and other enterprise data.

Weak security means attackers could disable all of a city's public EV chargers

US regulator tells GM to hit the brakes on customer tracking

21K Nissan customers' data stolen in Red Hat raid

Porsche panic in Russia as pricey status symbols forget how to car

Oracle has said little publicly about the reported attacks and didn't respond to The Register's questions, even as organizations have continued to disclose being caught in the fallout.

Nissan has not confirmed that the incidents are connected, though its California filing lists the breach period as May 27 through June 9, broadly aligning with the previously reported timeline.

The carmaker didn't respond to questions about how many current and former employees are affected, when Oracle first notified it of the breach, and whether the compromise was limited to Oracle-managed systems. ®

items.title: Dear IT Pros: I’m Begging You Not to Call Out Sick on GTA Day
items.content:
Grand Theft Auto VI will finally be released on Thursday, and it’s shaping up to be a historic event, with universally positive reviews . Kotaku calls the game “almost embarrassingly expensive and extravagant,” and it’s already made $1.65 billion in preorders.

There are stories of businesses giving their employees the day off to play the game and others where workers are taking several days off from their jobs to enjoy it. But if you work in IT, we implore you… don’t do that.

Everyone is aware of the outages at this point. Last week we saw air travel grind to a halt with only the second nationwide ground stop since the terror attacks of 9/11. Microsoft products like Outlook stopped working. And this week we saw outages at Chase that ripped through the banking system and a United outage just a few days after the FAA ground stop.

Rockstar’s latest open-world adventure is incredible, overwhelming, exciting, and different than any past GTA game

Some Apple services were also struggling on Tuesday, including iCloud and Apple Pay. Then there are the outages you probably didn’t even hear about, like the court portals that went down in California, Nevada, and Washington. The fact that Iran seems to have hacked energy tankers in August heading for the U.S. also didn’t get much coverage.

U.S. officials insist these most recent outages aren’t a result of cyberattacks by geopolitical adversaries like Iran, China, or Russia, nor are they coming from hackers looking to make a quick buck. The Washington Sun reported on Tuesday that bank CEOs and the NSA have told Congress some of the disruptions stem from attempts to patch systems where AI has identified vulnerabilities. And that’s where you good folks who work in IT come in.

We need you to stay on the job Thursday. It sucks; we get it. Who wouldn’t want to take a few days off from work to play the most important game of the decade? But we need you to have your head on a swivel right now. Because the AI bros are warning us that this is only going to get worse before it gets better.

Jason Clinton, Deputy Chief Information Security Officer at Anthropic, recently said as much in a post on X about the “vulnerability tsunami.” Clinton argues that we just need to get through the next 18 months and AI will be so good at making software without vulnerabilities that we can all take a breath. But we’re going to be white-knuckling it through the next year and a half at least.

as bad as things have gotten in the past 4 days, they are going to get a lot worse before they get better. security leaders, never let a crisis go to waste: please go to your boards and ask for help right now. not for ai, for the basics. (we need to hold on for ~18 months.) https://t.co/bcZp4heDtS

— Jason D. Clinton 🔸 (@JasonDClinton) October 22, 2026

Even if guys like Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin admit these most recent outages aren’t coming from near-peer adversaries, they do admit many of those same countries are trying to hack us. The U.S. is still engaged in a hot war with Iran, even if that’s fallen out of the headlines.

Mullin testified to the House Homeland Security Committee on Wednesday that, “Since February, Iranian activity has increasingly targeted the transportation, healthcare, water, energy, and financial services sectors.” February was, of course, when the U.S. and Israel launched a war of choice without any clear objective.

What’s publicly known about those threats is scary enough. Iran-linked hackers targeted water treatment facilities in the U.S. over the summer, with three dozen attempts in Minnesota alone. President Trump suggested at the time that state officials had attacked its own water infrastructure, a claim so stupid it feels insulting to even mention that it’s not true.

items.title: Day 14 - Who has permission?
items.content:
Files on a Linux system always have associated “permissions” - controlling who has access and what sort of access. You’ll have bumped into this in various ways already - as an example, yesterday while logged in as your “ordinary” user, you could not upload files directly into /var/www or create a new folder at / .

The Linux permission system is quite simple, but it does have some quirky and subtle aspects, so today is simply an introduction to some of the basic concepts.

This time you really do need to work your way through the material in the RESOURCES section!

First let’s look at “ownership”. All files are tagged with both the name of the user and the group that owns them, so if we type ls -l and see a file listing like this:

- rw ------- 1 steve staff 4478979 6 Feb 2011 private . txt

- rw - rw - r -- 1 steve staff 4478979 6 Feb 2011 press . txt

- rwxr - xr - x 1 steve staff 4478979 6 Feb 2011 upload . bin

Then these files are owned by user “steve”, and the group “staff”. Anyone that is not “steve” or is not part of the group “staff” is considered “other”. Others may still have permissions to handle these files, but they do not have any ownership.

If you want to change the ownership of a file, use the chown utility. This will change the user owner of file to a new user:

You can also change user and group at the same time:

If you only need to change the group owner, you can use chgrp command instead:

Since you created new users in the previous lesson, switch logins and create a few files to their home directories for testing. See how they show with ls -l

Looking at the -rw-r--r-- at the start of a directory listing line, (ignore the first “-” for now), and see these as potentially three groups of “rwx”: the permission granted to the “user” who owns the file, the “group”, and “other people” - we like to call that UGO .

private.txt - Steve has rw (ie Read and Write) permission, but neither the group “staff” nor “other people” have any permission at all

press.txt - Steve can Read and Write to this file too, but so can any member of the group “staff” and anyone , i.e. “other people”, can read it

upload.bin - Steve has rwx , he can read, write and execute - i.e. run this program - but the group and others can only read and execute it

You can change the permissions on any file with the chmod utility. Create a simple text file in your home directory with vim (e.g. tuesday.txt ) and check that you can list its contents by typing: cat tuesday.txt or less tuesday.txt .

Now look at its permissions by doing: ls -ltr tuesday.txt

-rw-rw-r-- 1 ubuntu ubuntu 12 Nov 19 14:48 tuesday.txt

So, the file is owned by the user “ubuntu”, and group “ubuntu”, who are the only ones that can write to the file - but any other user can only read it.

Now let’s remove the permission of the user and “ubuntu” group to write their own file:

…and remove the permission for “others” to read the file:

-r--r----- 1 ubuntu ubuntu 12 Nov 19 14:48 tuesday.txt

…and confirm by trying to edit the file with nano or vim . You’ll find that you appear to be able to edit it - but can’t save any changes. (In this case, as the owner, you have “permission to override permissions”, so can can write with :w! ). You can of course easily give yourself back the permission to write to the file by:

Just for fun, create a file: secret.txt in your home folder, take away all permissions from it for the user, group and others - and see what happens when you try to edit it with vim .

If all of this is old news to you, you may want to look into Linux ACLs:

How to Use the chown Command to Change the Owner of a File in Linux

items.title_ko: 14일차 - 누가 권한을 가지는가?
items.summary_ko: Linux 시스템의 모든 파일은 접근 권한이 연관되어 있으며, 이는 누가 접근할 수 있고 어떤 종류의 접근이 가능한지를 제어한다. Linux 권한 시스템은 단순하지만 미묘한 측면들이 있다.
items.content_ko: 모든 파일은 소유자(사용자) 및 그룹으로 태깅된다. ls -l 명령으로 파일 목록을 보면 사용자와 그룹을 확인할 수 있다. 예를 들어 'steve' 사용자와 'staff' 그룹이 파일을 소유한 경우, steve 또는 staff 그룹에 속하지 않은 사람은 '기타(other)'로 분류된다. 기타 사용자들도 파일에 대한 권한을 가질 수 있지만 소유권은 갖지 않는다. 권한 문자열의 각 자리(rwx)는 읽기, 쓰기, 실행 권한을 나타낸다.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

제가 집에서 한 말이나 제 언니랑 한 말들을 학교 가면 다 알고있어요 그래서 제가 말한 내용이랑 똑같은 내용을 꼭 제가 들을 수 있을때 언급하고 남자애들 여자애들 할것없이 제가 안보이는 데에서 조금만 이상한 말 하면 비웃으면서 지나가요 ㅠ 제가 진짜 친구가 없어서 학교에서 한마디도 안하는 날들이 대부분인데 제가 언니랑 학교 구석에서 말한 내용이랑 집에서 혼잣말 한 내용들을 똑같이 언급한게 한두번이 아니에요 ㅠ 제가 그냥 내용만 겹치면 말을 않겠는데 제가 말했던 내용 언급하면서 꼭 제 이름도 한번씩 부르고 그래요 보통 사람들은 자기이름을 그렇게 말하면 기분나빠서 한번 돌아보기라도 하겠지만 저는 성격이 워낙 내성적이라 누가 비웃고 지나가거나 째려보거나 저 보면서 한숨쉬어도 아무말도 못하거든요 ㅠ 그래서 그냥 기분만 나쁜건데 이게 하루이틀 쌓이니까 너무 힘들더라고요 ㅠ 처음엔 저도 이게 정신이 약간 아픈건가 했는데 정신병 관련 영상도 다 보고 그랬는데 환청은 이런식으로 들리는게 아니라고 하더라고요 계속 날 비난하고 그런식으로 들리는건데 저는 그런게 전혀 아니라 제가 전날 했던 얘기들, 방금 쉬는시간에 학교 구석에서 나눈 얘기들을 자꾸 똑같이 언급하니까 미치겠어요 ㅠ 한두번 우연으로 겹치는게 아니라 계속 겹쳐요 진짜.. 그리고 애초에 제가 학교에서 말을 한마디도 안하는데 자꾸 저한테 그런 반응을 보인다는게 애초에 저한테 이상한 일이 일어난다는 반증 아닌가요? 그리고 걔네가 말했던걸 몇개를 말씀드려보면 제가 도청을 의심한 초기에 급식실에서 밥먹고있었는데 어떤 남자애가 “도청” 이러고 지나가는거에요 그리고 저희반 남자애가 제 언니 이동수업반이랑 같은 반인데 거기서 쉬는시간에 “도청기를 달고다녀 ㅋㅋㅋㅋ” 이랬다는거에요 진짜 이상하죠 저는 예전에 우울증 약을 먹은적이 있어서 정신이 막 무결점으로 건강한 편은 아니에요 근데 저희 언니는 그런적도 없고 교우관계도 좋고 진짜 정신이 건강하거든요 ㅠ 근데 저희 언니가 그런말을 들었다니깐 진짜 도청이 일어나는게 맞는거구나 생각했어요.. 그리고 또 있었던 일을 말씀드리면 이동수업 때 제 뒷쪽에서 남자애가 제 아버지 직업을 언급하면서 제 이름을 말하는거에요 이게 도청을 하지 않고서는 절대 알수가 없는 사실이거든요 ㅠ 또 “정신병ㅋㅋㅋ” 하면서 제 이름을 언급하는거에요 이것도 도청을 하지 않았다면 알수 없는거고요 더 말씀드릴 사례가 많은데 그러면 너무 길어져서 이정도만 말씀드릴게요 그래서 찾아보니까 머리에 붙일수 있는 초소형 도청기가 있다길래  제 언니가 제 머리를 샅샅이 뒤져줬거든요? 근데 그래도 아무것도 안나오더라고요 ㅠ 그리고 또 도청 탐지 업체를 알아보니까 금액이 너무 비싸서요 ㅠ 제가 고3인데 이런일을 당해서 너무 스트레스 받는데 방법이 없어서 정말 어떻게 해야될지 모르겠어요 안그래도 제가 여자애들이나 남자애들이 괴롭힐 소재가 많은 조용한 애거든요 ㅠ그래서 저를 지나칠때 꼭 한마디 끼얹고 지나가고 그래서 학교생활이 막 편한 그런애는 아닌데 학교에서 유일하게 맘놓고 말할 수 있는 언니랑 말하는 얘기를 다 알고있으니까 스트레스 받아서 공부 능력도 점점 떨어지는것같고 쨋든 걱정이 이만저만이 아니에요 어떡해야되죠 ㅠㅠ 제가 성격이 활발한 편도 아니고 집에 돈이 많지도 않아서 진짜 대학 잘가야되는데 걱정이에요ㅠㅠ 긴글 읽어주셔서 감사하고요 여기가 사생활 침해 관련한 갤러리니까 혹여나 저랑 비슷한 경험이 있으시거나 관련 지식이 있는 분은 제가 어떻게 해야하는건지 알려주시면 진짜진짜 감사드릴것같아요 많은 도움 부탁드려요 정말 방법 여러가지 찾아봐도 안되겠어서 여기다 글 남겨요

items.title: Energy-Based Reasoners: 385x more efficient inference
items.content:
Looping is a powerful inductive bias for reasoning. By repeatedly iterating a recurrent block, looped models can scale their effective depth and enable multi-step reasoning in latent space. However, existing looped models are not inherently guided by an explicit measure of progress, making it difficult to determine when to stop looping and how to improve upon the current state. To enable this, we introduce Energy-Based Reasoners ( EBRs ), which learn an energy function over latent reasoning states and formulate looped updates as gradient descent on this energy. The energy scores latent states, while its gradient guides refinement and provides a signal for stopping. To train EBRs effectively, we further introduce exploration-based training to discover additional modes and to better shape the energy landscape over a broader set of states. Across four algorithmic reasoning benchmarks, EBRs match or outperform prior recurrent reasoning models, achieving 99.9% accuracy on Sudoku-Extreme while using 345× less inference compute than the next-best model and maintaining comparable training compute. On all multi-solution benchmarks, EBRs achieve state-of-the-art coverage of distinct valid solutions while maintaining near-100% single-sample accuracy. These results suggest that energy-based models are a promising approach for strong reasoning performance.

Existing looped reasoners update their latent state without any explicit assessment of it. An EBR learns an energy function that guides refinement, stopping and selection.

Score. The energy rates the compatibility between the reasoning state z and the initial board x . Lower means better compatibility.

Refine. The gradient turns the score into an improvement direction.

Stop. The state becomes stationary once the gradient is small, so the gradient acts as a stopping criterion.

Select. Among multiple candidate solutions, we pick the one with the lowest energy.

Correct solutions settle at low-energy stationary states. Energy, gradient norm and step size during descent on Sudoku-Extreme. Correct trajectories settle at low energy with small gradients, while wrong ones keep moving.

Running more descent steps refines each answer further, and running more trajectories gives the energy more candidates to choose the lowest-energy one from.

EBRs reach EqR's best accuracy with 7× fewer iterations (left) and 43× fewer samples (right).

GRAM and TRM from GRAM's paper; EqR from its released checkpoint. Mean ± SD over three seeds.

Each trajectory stops once its energy gradient falls below a threshold, so easy puzzles finish in a few steps and hard ones keep going.

EBRs give the best single-sample accuracy among reasoning models. Within only 5 passes, they reach 99.9% and 88.3%, ahead of methods that draw up to 128. Stopping each trajectory once its energy gradient falls below a threshold keeps 99.9% accuracy with 10.9× fewer FLOPs than a fixed-depth EBR, allowing us to surpass EqR with 345× fewer FLOPs.

EBR acts like stochastic gradient descent and can capture many different solutions. Coverage captures the share of each input's distinct valid solutions that 20 samples find.

Pass@1 (%) and Conflicts (edges summed over the test graphs) use one sample. Cov@20 is the share of distinct valid solutions found by 20 samples (%). Baselines from GRAM's paper.
items.title_ko: 에너지 기반 추론기(EBR), 차선 모델 대비 추론 연산 345배 절감
items.summary_ko: Energy-Based Reasoners(EBR)는 잠재 추론 상태에 대한 에너지 함수를 학습하고, 반복 업데이트를 이 에너지의 경사 하강으로 구성하는 모델이다. 네 가지 알고리즘 추론 벤치마크에서 기존 반복 추론 모델과 같거나 더 나은 성능을 보였으며, Sudoku-Extreme에서 99.9%의 정확도를 기록했다. 본문에 따르면 차선 모델보다 추론 연산을 345배 적게 사용했다.
items.content_ko: 반복 연산은 추론에 강력한 귀납적 편향이 된다. 그러나 기존 반복 모델은 진행 정도를 측정하는 명시적 기준이 없어 언제 멈출지, 현재 상태를 어떻게 개선할지 판단하기 어렵다. 이를 해결하기 위해 저자들은 잠재 추론 상태 위에 에너지 함수를 학습하고, 반복 업데이트를 이 에너지의 경사 하강으로 정의한 Energy-Based Reasoners(EBR)를 제안한다. 에너지는 상태를 점수화하고, 그 기울기는 상태 개선 방향과 멈춤 신호를 준다. 또한 여러 해를 발견하고 더 넓은 상태 공간에서 에너지 지형을 다듬기 위해 탐색 기반 학습을 도입했다. 네 가지 알고리즘 추론 벤치마크에서 EBR은 기존 반복 추론 모델과 같거나 더 나은 성능을 보였다. Sudoku-Extreme에서는 99.9%의 정확도를 기록하면서도 차선 모델보다 추론 연산을 345배 적게 썼고, 학습 연산량은 비슷하게 유지했다. 다중 해 벤치마크 결과의 나머지 내용은 원문이 잘려 있다.

items.title: Upcoming Critical PHP Security Release (18 Nov 2026)
items.summary: php, security
items.content:
PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 fix two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution. All PHP users are strongly encouraged to update immediately.

Who is at risk: all PHP installations serving web requests, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed. We consider the risk highest for mod_php, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs.

RCE via OOM corruption , CVE-2026-109618 ( GHSA-w8hw-w9fx-j79w ): out-of-memory

handling can interrupt PHP while internal request data is only partially initialized. Request cleanup may then treat the invalid data as valid.

RCE via stale global state , CVE-2026-109619 ( GHSA-6wmf-4rv5-p3rp ): request-owned

internal state can survive after its backing memory has been freed. A later request handled by the same worker may use that stale state before normal initialization resets it.

Update to PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35. Source downloads are on our downloads page . Windows source and binaries are on the same page .

Linux distributions and LTS vendors received the patches in advance, so check your vendor for updated packages.

PHP 8.1 and older no longer receive updates from the PHP project. Some distributions and LTS vendors provide backported fixes, so contact your vendor for details, or upgrade to a supported version.

Given the severity of these vulnerabilities, the PHP security team provided minimal source-backports for PHP 7.4 , PHP 8.0 , and PHP 8.1 to help people building from source or without access to an LTS vendor.

If you cannot update immediately: while only an update is a complete solution, the following measures reduce exposure to specific attack paths but do not make an installation safe.

RCE via OOM corruption (CVE-2026-109618):

Set memory_limit=-1 , preferably in a way applications can't override, such as php_admin_value in the FPM pool or Apache configuration, and check that no pool, directory or application setting puts a finite limit back. This removes the controllable PHP memory limit failure, but an underlying allocation failure can still reach the vulnerable path.

Set a low post_max_size . For applications that don't require file uploads, set post_max_size = 8M . If file uploads are necessary, set post_max_size = 32M . Keep upload_max_filesize below post_max_size .

Consider enforcing limits at the web server or proxy level for decoded request size, input field count, multipart part count, header count, and nesting depth. These

limits must also cover requests without a usable Content-Length .

Use a container or cgroup limit as an availability boundary, preferably with a policy that kills only the affected worker. Do not substitute RLIMIT_AS or

RLIMIT_DATA , as these can cause the vulnerable allocation failure.

RCE via stale global state (CVE-2026-109619):

Set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 and restart every worker. Use php.ini , an FPM pool or server

configuration that applies before request parsing. Do not rely on ini_set() or FPM .user.ini . This blocks the confirmed session paths but not other variants.

On PHP 8.5, set fatal_error_backtraces=0 and restart every worker. This blocks the confirmed fatal backtrace path only.

Remove invalid or deprecated settings applied per request that emit diagnostics before initialization. Hiding diagnostics with error_reporting , display_errors

Fix attacker-reachable fatal errors and execution timeouts, including failures in callbacks, upload or import processing and cleanup.

The advisories linked above have the full technical details.

items.title: Chinese Hackers Abused Google Workspace Rules to Steal Research and Defense Emails
items.content:
A China-linked espionage group hid inside North American medical, academic, and military research networks for more than a year, quietly stealing sensitive research and defense email.

The way in was a backdoor on their REDCap research servers that stole login credentials. The exfiltration was the unusual part: the attackers rewired the victims' own Google Workspace rules to copy any message matching their keywords to an inbox they controlled.

Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) laid out the campaign in a report published this week and attributes it with high confidence to a cluster it tracks as UNC6508.

The actor and its REDCap backdoor are not new names; Google first surfaced both in February , in a wider report on state-backed attacks against the defense sector. It did not name the victims, describing them only as multiple organizations across the US and Canada: clinical providers, academic centers, military health institutions, advocacy groups, and health regulators.

Google says it notified them and disrupted the group's infrastructure.

The entry point was REDCap (Research Electronic Data Capture), a web platform that hospitals and universities use to build and manage study databases. UNC6508 compromised externally facing REDCap servers.

Google has not pinned down the initial access vector, named a specific CVE, or listed the affected versions, though it saw the group probing older, vulnerable ones.

Around three months after getting in, the group deployed custom malware GTIG calls INFINITERED , which trojanizes REDCap's own system files and does three things.

The earliest known compromise dates to September 2023, with activity continuing through November 2025. Once on the server, UNC6508 ran internal reconnaissance and credential discovery, pulling database and service account credentials, then used those logins to move into the internal network and on to a domain administrator account.

Google does not spell out the exact path to that admin account. With admin rights, the group set up the exfiltration.

The exfiltration rode a feature that was already there. UNC6508 abused content compliance rules, a legitimate Google Workspace admin feature that scans mail for keywords and can copy or forward matching messages.

Similar features exist in other cloud mail suites. The group created a rule, misspelled "Patroit," that watched for nearly 150 keywords, search terms, and email addresses. When a message matched, Workspace silently BCC'd it to an attacker-controlled Gmail address, which Google has since disabled. No malware on the mail server, no separate exfiltration tool, no unusual network traffic. Just a built-in mail feature, turned to copy the organization's secrets to an inbox the attackers owned.

MITRE already catalogs email-forwarding-rule abuse as a known technique. What GTIG flags as new here is the use of domain content compliance rules to do it, a method it says it had not seen from a China-linked actor before.

The rule's keywords mapped to UNC6508's collection priorities: geo-strategic policy, military strategy and equipment, advanced technology including AI and uncrewed vehicles, offensive cyber programs, and medical research. One term stood out for its specificity, chikungunya , the mosquito-borne virus behind a 2025 outbreak in China's Guangdong province.

Start with REDCap. Patch externally facing servers and remove old versions outright, not just alongside the current build. REDCap lets legacy versions run side-by-side, and that is what enables downgrade attacks, where an attacker forces software back to a known-vulnerable release.

Then check the mail side. Review Workspace, or equivalent, content compliance and mail-forwarding rules for anything that BCCs or reroutes mail to outside addresses. Check admin audit logs for when rules changed, not just what they say now. Pull GTIG's published indicators and hunt for INFINITERED. items.title: Virginia is responsible for about a quarter of the total electricity used by data centers in the U.S. and a third of their carbon emissions
items.content:
Study reveals just how much energy Virginia’s data centers use

Published November 17, 2026 at 2:33 PM EST

A large data center facility with multiple buildings and cooling units in Virginia.

Electricity consumed by the Commonwealth’s major data centers is enough to power roughly 2 million homes.

Virginia is responsible for about a quarter of the total electricity used by data centers in the U.S. — and a third of their carbon emissions, according to a major report published Monday .

Researchers at Harvard University’s T.H. Chan School of Public Health and Data Science Initiative calculated energy use and climate pollution from data centers nationwide between May 2024 and April 2025.

These massive “computer farms” account for about 1.8% of the country’s total electricity consumption, the study found. Together, they use as much energy as some U.S. states, including Michigan and Tennessee.

“Data centers are growing incredibly fast, driven largely by AI, and decisions about where to build them and how to power them are being made right now,” lead author Gianluca Guidi said in a statement.

“But there’s very little facility-level information about their environmental footprint. Our study helps fill that gap.”

The report comes as data centers face increasing public pushback over concerns about environmental impacts, community disruption and skyrocketing electricity bills.

Some Virginia lawmakers are pushing for a three-year moratorium on building data centers, and several Hampton Roads cities have passed or are considering similar bans.

Virginia is known as the data center capital of the world, with each facility housing hundreds of thousands or even millions of computer servers, which require lots of energy to power and cool.

Harvard researchers used satellite imagery and industry research to assemble a dataset of 403 hyperscale data centers. Virginia had the most by a wide margin at 142, followed by Oregon at 56.

The report found Virginia’s facilities used 21.4 terawatt-hours of electricity over the course of the year, or enough to power roughly 2 million homes.

A majority of large data centers rely on fossil fuels, especially natural gas, according to the report. That releases planet-warming gas emissions into the atmosphere, contributing to climate change.

Researchers attributed carbon emissions to each facility based on the power sources in their region. In areas with a higher share of renewable electricity, such as the Pacific Northwest, each data center is responsible for a lesser amount of emissions.

The Mid-Atlantic’s power mix is about 46% natural gas, 33% nuclear, 14% coal and 7% renewables.

Accordingly, Virginia’s data centers were estimated to emit 7 million metric tons of carbon dioxide in the year studied — equivalent to about 7% of the state’s total carbon emissions.

The Sierra Club this week released a separate report stating that data centers are “on track to erase 15 years of U.S. climate progress,” as power companies invest in more fossil fuel infrastructure to accommodate growing demand from the computer warehouses.

Meanwhile, PJM Interconnection, which oversees the electric grid in Virginia and a dozen other states, has been trying to curb the outsized impact of data centers on residential electric bills. (As the industry uses more power, companies such as Dominion Energy build more power plants and pass those costs on to all customers.)

PJM recently sought to make several changes , including forcing data centers to supply their own power or risk being cut off during peak demand.

The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission largely rejected that proposal, but PJM recently announced a new plan that could require data center companies to pay a larger share of grid costs.

items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

items.title: AI agents ask better questions than KPMG accountants in audit trial
items.content:
LONDON, November 18, 2026 — Artificial intelligence has taken another significant step into the world of professional services after KPMG revealed that AI agents examining the accounts of a major UK-listed company sometimes investigated financial issues more deeply and asked better questions than its human audit team.

The experiment, conducted by KPMG UK using more than 100 AI agents, marks an important development in the application of artificial intelligence to one of the most labour-intensive areas of the financial services industry. It also raises an uncomfortable question for the accountancy profession: if machines can increasingly perform the analytical work traditionally undertaken by highly trained professionals, how quickly will the economics of auditing change?

According to the Financial Times , the project, codenamed Project Exponential, examined the financial statements of an unnamed FTSE 250 company. The AI agents worked alongside a conventional audit team, undertaking tasks across the audit process rather than simply assisting with isolated administrative functions.

KPMG UK head of audit Cath Burnet said the technology had, in several instances, gone considerably deeper into issues than the regular audit team, identifying areas requiring further investigation and asking questions that human auditors had not necessarily raised.

The findings suggest that AI’s potential in professional services may extend well beyond improving productivity. It could fundamentally change how complex financial information is examined, interpreted and challenged.

From supporting accountants to conducting audits

Project Exponential represents a shift from using AI as a supporting tool towards deploying autonomous agents across an entire audit workflow.

The agents collected information, analysed and documented data, developed draft conclusions and observations, and suggested subsequent steps. They were also able to work alongside one another, effectively dividing responsibilities and coordinating elements of the investigation.

The technology was developed over approximately four months. However, KPMG was careful to distinguish the experiment from a formally approved statutory audit. Although an audit partner signed off on the experimental exercise, its findings were not used as the basis for formally approving the company’s accounts.

Human oversight remained essential. During the trial, an auditor had to intervene when one AI agent failed to correctly match regulatory requirements with the company’s documentation. The episode illustrates both the capabilities and limitations of current AI systems when dealing with complex regulatory frameworks.

KPMG plans to expand the initiative to as many as 20 larger audits, although the firm acknowledges that the technology is not yet sufficiently mature to be deployed across thousands of engagements. Data quality also remains a significant obstacle, with some businesses lacking the clean, structured information required for AI agents to operate effectively.

A challenge to the Big Four business model?

The implications for the accountancy industry could be substantial.

Traditional auditing relies on large teams of junior accountants undertaking detailed and repetitive work, supervised by experienced managers and partners. AI agents potentially offer a different operating model, automating significant portions of data collection, analysis and documentation while allowing senior professionals to concentrate on complex judgements and exceptions.

For firms such as KPMG, Deloitte, PwC and EY, the attraction is clear: faster audits, potentially lower operating costs and the ability to analyse much larger volumes of financial information.
